newsitem.title: UK: PFI essential to cope with UK prison demand -Straw.
newsitem.headline: PFI essential to cope with UK prison demand -Straw.

text.p: Home Secretary Jack Straw said on Tuesday that although he was against privately-run prisons in principle, he believed a fast-rising demand for places in cells in the UK could not be satisfied without them.

Straw told parliament's Home Affairs Committee: "Given the very low level of the prison capital allocation in the public expenditure totals, the only way that prison allocation can be provided is through the Private Finance Initiative (PFI)."
He said that for the moment, the PFI would include the management of prisons as well as their design, building and financing.
Straw told the committee the prison population had risen 40 percent over the past five years to 62,000, and the 2,500 increase since May 1 was 1,700 more than had been expected.
He last week announced extra public finance of 43 million stg to help cope with the swelling prison numbers.
"I believe in principle that the incarceration of prisoners should be a direct function of the state," he said.
But he added: "Some of the anxieties which were widely shared when private prisons began (in Britain) are somewhat less than they were." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
